findings.finding: The reference is the original receptor-bound ligand pose, with 25 heavy atoms, and is explicitly not a generated Steer structure. No affinity labels are supplied, so this geometry alone does not establish potency or enrichment.

The ligand covariance eigenvalues (0.111, 5.696, 9.303 Å²) indicate a comparatively narrow dimension and two broader dimensions in the observed pose; this is a geometric observation, not evidence that a particular shape should be optimized.

The supplied bound-pose proxy reports close ligand neighborhoods around LEU45, ILE174, VAL66, VAL53, PHE113, HIS160, MET163, VAL116, ASP175, and HIS115. These are untyped distance/Gaussian-shell summaries, not chemically typed interactions or energetic contributions.

The strongest listed proxy sums include PHE113 (18.71), LEU45 (16.93), and ILE174 (16.52), while listed ligand-atom counts within 4.5 Å range from 3 to 10. This describes the observed pose only; it does not identify causal anchors or an optimum.

The receptor crop contains 308 heavy atoms within a 12 Å crop radius. Its reported nearest-neighbor quantiles include distances as short as 1.23 Å, so the input crop geometry warrants steric scrutiny; the summary does not identify which atoms or whether these are true clashes.

directions: As a testable design hypothesis, compare small contact_weight changes (0.1, 0.25, 0.5) against the current setting while holding other supported parameters fixed; assess final predicted pIC50 and strain on matched runs rather than treating the bound-pose proxy as a target optimum.

Probe repulsion_weight values (1, 2, 4) to test whether reducing close-contact penalties improves final predictions and pose plausibility; inspect atom-level geometry because the supplied crop summary cannot localize short-distance pairs.

Compare ligand_anchor_weight 0.5, 1, and 2 as an explicit test of dependence on the original bound pose, with graph transitions allowed and outcomes evaluated using the stated pIC50 objective. This is applicable to the structure formula only.

Evaluate native_rms_ratio (0.1, 0.2, 0.33) and time_ramp_power (0, 1, 2) as separate controlled ablations; these are candidate settings, not statistically supported improvements from the supplied evidence.
limitations: Only structure-level evidence is provided. No generated molecules, scored outcomes, affinity labels, baseline comparison, or replicate statistics are supplied; enrichment, selection survival, temporal trends, and parameter effects cannot be estimated.

The receptor-bound ligand and contact summaries describe one reference pose. Contacts are untyped geometric proxies, with no interaction or energy labels, and cannot establish binding strength or causal residue contributions.

The evidence manifest is explicitly a compressed exploratory selection of strongest 8 and weakest 2 q-values per supplied table, not a complete enrichment analysis; no q-value table or comparisons are included in this call.

D3 removes lineage, temporal, elite-geometry, and history-matching instruction blocks. The execution metadata also says particle selection is false and affinity-head gradients are absent; conclusions about those unavailable signals are unsupported.

Candidate settings are constrained by the supplied allowed_updates and formula registry. The pocket formula has no ligand-anchor update; the structure formula can include it. Any claimed improvement requires generated evaluation against matched controls.
